critical.issue: Returns 422 for partial updates. ClassConfigIn.name is required (no default), so sending only e.g. {description:'x'} fails Pydantic validation. Spec requires partial update.

minor.issue: Cascading from above: 'class.updated' entry never appears in the log because PATCH /api/class currently 422s on partial payloads.

Theme subtitle 'Segue automaticamente le impostazioni del sistema.' remains Italian after switching to English — missing EN translation.

critical_code_review_comments: ClassConfigIn is reused for both POST /class/setup (creation) and PATCH /class (partial update). Since name is required, the schema cannot support partial updates. Split into ClassCreateIn / ClassPatchIn.
server.py is ~980 lines; consider splitting into routers (auth, class, chat, homework, etc.) per code_review_guidelines (>700 line threshold).

PATCH /users/{id} uses body.dict() without exclude_unset, which sends None for unspecified fields. That would overwrite existing muted/role/disabled with None. In practice this test passed because only the intended field was included, but it's fragile — switch to body.dict(exclude_unset=True).

rca_of_issue: PATCH /api/class 422 RCA: In server.py line 182, `class ClassConfigIn` defines `name: str` as required. The PATCH handler (line 483) uses this same model, so FastAPI/Pydantic rejects any payload missing 'name'. Reproduction: `curl -X PATCH $URL/api/class -H 'Authorization: Bearer <admin>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"description":"x"}'` → 422. Mitigation: add a dedicated ClassPatchIn with all Optional fields, or make `name: Optional[str] = None` on ClassConfigIn (with an explicit not-null check in POST /class/setup). Then PATCH /api/class's `body.dict(exclude_unset=True)` will correctly persist only the supplied fields, and _log_admin('class.updated', upd) will begin appearing in admin_log.
